Here are some of the journal and conference papers I have published or are in the works. For a complete list of my publications, feel free to check out my Google Scholar page.

Numerically computing safe, invariant sets for general dynamical systems using SOS programming
Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar, Michael Otte
in preparation for Letters in Control Systems (L-CSS)

[Paper in preparation]


Funnels are finite-time invariant sets, quite useful in feedback motion planning to guarantee safety and stabilisability. This work aims to compute funnels for nonlinear dynamical systems using Lyapunov theory and semi-algebraic programming. For systems with polynomial vector fields, it leverages sum-of-squares (SOS) programming for computational efficiency.
Cross-Attention-Based Multimodal Representation Fusion for Parametric Gait Adaptation in Complex Terrains
G Seneviratne, K Weerakoon, M Elnoor, V Rajgopal, H Varatharajan, MKM Jaffar, J Pusey, D Manocha
under review for IROS, 2025

[Project Page] [arXiv] [Video]


This algorithm for quadruped robots uses cross attention to fuse terrain representations derived from visual and proprioceptive inputs for gait adjustment. The cross-attention mechanism selects and integrates the most relevant features from each modality to adaptively adjust the robot's gait in response to varying terrains such as asphalt, grass, dense vegetation, gravel, and sand.
A Failsafe Framework to Control a Quadrotor despite Multiple Rotor Failures
Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar, Michael Otte
in preparation for Journal of Guidance, Control, and Dynamics (JGCD)

[Manuscript in preparation]


This work proposes nonlinear control policies for position tracking in quadrotors that have lost one, two-opposite, or even three rotors. The strategy is to control the axis about which the faulty vehicle spins, referred to as reduced attitude, and tilt this axis to steer the post-fault vehicle towards the desired position. A key contribution of this work is its motion control strategy to safely land a quadrotor with just one functional rotor.
Robot Navigation Using Physically Grounded Vision-Language Models in Outdoor Environments
M Elnoor, K Weerakoon, G Seneviratne, R Xian, T Guan, MKM Jaffar, V Rajagopal, D Manocha
to appear at ICRA, 2025

[Project Page] [arXiv] [Video]


To make mobile robots capable of handling diverse terrain conditions, this work uses vision-language models (VLMs) integrated with physical grounding to assess terrains' intrinsic properties such as deformability and slipperiness. It uses proprioceptive-based sensing to estimate the terrain's physical properties, and those subsequently inform both the local and global planners for real-time trajectory replanning.
BehAV: Behavioral Rule Guided Autonomy Using VLMs for Robot Navigation in Outdoor Scenes
K Weerakoon, M Elnoor, G Seneviratne, V Rajagopal, SH Arul, J Liang, MKM Jaffar, D Manocha
to appear at ICRA, 2025

[Project Page] [arXiv] [Video]


This work leverages Vision Language Models (VLMs) for autonomous robot navigation in outdoor scenes guided by human instructions. Human commands are interpreted using LLMs and categorized into navigation instructions and behavioral guidelines. Based on the guidelines, a behavioral cost map is computed and integrated with the occupancy map for navigation. To navigate in dynamic outdoor settings, an unconstrained MPC-based planner that prioritizes both reaching landmarks and following behavioral guidelines is used.
Trajectory Tracking while Stabilizing an Inverted Pendulum on a Quadcopter Using Adaptive Model-Predictive Control
Han Yang, Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar, Michael W Otte
AIAA SciTech Forum, 2024

[Paper] [Preprint]


We combine the canonical problem of stabilizing an inverted pendulum with quadcopter trajectory tracking to study the control of 'flying inverted pendulum'. This work presents an adaptive model-predictive controller strategy to control this UAV model. A nominal nonlinear MPC is augmented with an L1 adaptive controller that performs online estimation of the modeling uncertainties, especially parameter mismatches, and continually compensates for it.
The Development of a Drag-Modulating Closed-loop Feedback System to Control a Rocket’s Ascent
Ezra Bregin, Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar
AIAA SciTech Forum, 2024

[Project Page] [Paper] [Preprint]


This paper presents a study on the development and experimental validation of an advanced air brake system for a sounding rocket. The primary objective of the air brake is to effectively modulate drag during the coast phase through a closed-loop feedback loop, thereby enabling apogee control. To achieve this, an EKF-based state-estimation scheme and a model predictive controller (MPC) are developed, tested, and experimentally validated.
Low-level controller in response to changes in quadrotor dynamics
JK Cho, C Kim, MKM Jaffar, M Otte, SW Kim
IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA), 2023

[Paper] [Preprint] [Video] [Code]


In this study, we focus on training a low-level controller using reinforcement learning (RL) that operates in response to dynamics changes without a priori knowledge or fine-tuning of the parameters. The quadrotor dynamics is randomized in simulator and the policy is trained on dynamics information extracted from the state-action history through recurrent neural networks (RNNs). Additionally, our experiments demonstrate shortcomings of applying actor-critic architecture that use end-to-end RNNs, for the specific case of uncertain dynamics.
PiP-X: Funnel-Based Online Feedback Motion Planning/Replanning in Dynamic Environments
Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar, Michael Otte
Workshop on the Algorithmic Foundations of Robotics, WAFR 2022
Also appears as a book chapter in Springer Proceedings in Advanced Robotics   Best Paper Award Consideration

[Book chapter] [arXiv] [Code]


We introduce an online sampling-based feedback motion re-planning algorithm using finite-time invariant sets – 'funnels'. This work combines concepts from nonlinear systems analysis, sampling-based motion planning, and graph-search to create a single framework that enables motion planning/replanning for general nonlinear systems in a dynamic workspace. One of the key contributions is a graph data structure to represent a network of volumetric funnels, enabling the use of D*Lite for quick graph rewiring in response to changes in obtacle space.
Experimental comparison of decentralized task allocation algorithms under imperfect communication
S Nayak, S Yeotikar, E Carrillo, E Rudnick-Cohen, MKM Jaffar, R Patel, S Azarm, J W Herrmann, H Xu, M Otte
IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters, 2020

[Paper] [Preprint]


We compare the performance of five state of the art decentralized task allocation algorithms under imperfect communication conditions. The decentralized algorithms we consider are CBAA, ACBBA, DHBA, HIPC and PI. All algorithms are evaluated using three different models of communication, including the Bernoulli model, the Gilbert-Elliot model, and the Rayleigh Fading model.
A novel guidance algorithm and comparison of nonlinear control strategies applied to an indoor quadrotor
Mohamed Khalid M Jaffar, Manoj Velmurugan, Ranjith Mohan
Fifth Indian Control Conference (ICC), 2019

[Paper] [Preprint]


In this paper we propose a cascaded approach for the full control of a quadrotor operating in indoor spaces. Sliding mode controller with a saturation function is applied to achieve robust attitude tracking performance without control chattering. The robustness and effectiveness of the proposed control law are validated through simulations and experiments under external disturbances.
